title: Adaptive DCS-SOMP for 5G Localization Parameter Estimation
subtitle: Core Argument Plan: From 3D Channel Modeling to Adaptive Sparse Recovery

nodes.title: Problem Definition: 3D Localization in Industry 4.0
nodes.purpose: Define the necessity of estimating five specific parameters (ToA, 2D-AoD, 2D-AoA) in 3D environments for applications like smart warehousing, and identify limitations of existing 2D or coarse-estimation methods.

nodes.title: System & Channel Model Formulation
nodes.purpose: Establish the mathematical foundation using 3GPP TR 38.901 guidelines, defining the MIMO mmWave channel matrix with UCA arrays and the relationship between received signals and localization parameters.

nodes.title: Sensing Matrix Construction & Complexity Bottleneck
nodes.purpose: Explain the construction of the initial sensing matrix via Kronecker products of array response vectors and demonstrate how candidate density ($q_{az}, q_{el}$) creates a memory and computational bottleneck.

nodes.title: Adaptive Search Mechanism (Core Innovation)
nodes.purpose: Detail the proposed algorithm's dynamic adjustment of the search space intervals ($[	ilde{	heta}_{start}, 	ilde{	heta}_{end}]$) based on previous iteration indices, allowing high resolution with low candidate counts per step.

nodes.title: Algorithmic Execution Flow
nodes.purpose: Trace the logical flow from residual calculation, maximum correlation search, index conversion to angles, and the iterative update loop defined in Algorithms 1 and 2.

nodes.title: Theoretical Complexity & Resource Analysis
nodes.purpose: Present the Big-O complexity comparison ($O(LN_t(q_c)^2)$ vs $O(LN_t q_c q_{it})$) and the formula for total mathematical operations to justify efficiency gains.

nodes.title: Empirical Validation: Accuracy and Speed
nodes.purpose: Analyze simulation results comparing execution time, operation counts, and RMSE metrics between standard DCS-SOMP and the proposed adaptive method across all five parameters.

nodes.title: Scope, Assumptions, and Future Work
nodes.purpose: Identify critical constraints such as perfect clock synchronization, single-bounce path assumptions, and proposed future enhancements like residue update refinement.

coverage_notes: The argument chain moves logically from the physical problem (3D localization needs) to the mathematical model, identifies the computational barrier in traditional CS, proposes the adaptive solution, and validates it theoretically and empirically.
Key variables ($N_t, N_r, q_{az}, q_{el}, K, L$) and formulas (Channel Matrix Eq. 1, Sensing Matrix Eq. 7, ToA Eq. 16, RMSE Eq. 27) are central to nodes 2, 3, 4, and 6.
Table 1 (Page 3) and Tables 3-4 (Page 11) provide the comparative evidence required for nodes 1 and 7.
